title: Phase-G test files placed in src/ instead of tests/, leaking vitest into production build output
what_happened: Phase G1/G2 created its two test files (sandbox.test.ts, core-isolation.test.ts) inside src/sandbox/ rather than the repo's tests/ directory. tsconfig.json has include:["src"] and exclude:["tests","bin","dist","scripts"], so `npm run build` (= tsc) compiled both test files into dist/sandbox/*.test.js + .d.ts + .js.map, and the emitted JS contained `import { describe, it, expect } from "vitest"` — a dev-only dependency in production build output. 6 stale artifacts were emitted before detection.
root_cause: Did not verify existing repo layout/convention before placing new test files. The repo has 17 pre-existing tests, all under tests/ (already excluded from the build); no *.test.ts existed anywhere under src/. The convention was discoverable from tsconfig exclude and the tests/ directory, and was not checked.
what_i_did_wrong: 1) Assumed colocated tests (src/foo/foo.test.ts) were acceptable without checking the project's own tsconfig and test layout. 2) Reported the fix as 'all tests pass, build clean' in the Phase G1/G2 report while `npm run build` was quietly emitting test files into dist/. 3) The report documented test paths that did not match repo convention.
detection: User prompted 'check repo, theres issue'. Independent recon found the mismatch: tsconfig include/exclude vs. actual test placement, and confirmed dist/sandbox/*.test.* containing vitest imports.
correction: Moved both test files to tests/ (matching repo convention), rewrote their relative imports, deleted the 6 stale dist artifacts. Config change (tsconfig) deliberately NOT made — the fix is relocation, honoring the Phase-G zero-core-modification constraint.
corrective_action: Before adding any new test file to a repo, inspect tsconfig include/exclude and the existing test directory layout first; place tests where the project already places them.
verification: npx tsc --noEmit -> 0; npx vitest run tests/sandbox.test.ts tests/core-isolation.test.ts -> 17/17; npm run build -> 0; recursive dist search for *.test.* -> 0 matches; git status -> no tracked file modified.
